newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU sale pressure on Cr Lyonnais - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: EU sale pressure on Cr Lyonnais - Le Monde.

text.p: European Commission competition policy officials would prefer to see French state bank Credit Lyonnais limit the sell-off of non-profitable networks and are not in favour of it holding on to all its profitable networks, according to afternoon daily Le Monde.

Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade met European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert on Monday about plans being drawn up for a restructuring in return for Commission approval of further French state aid for the bank.

It said the Commission was expecting a restructuring plan for the troubled bank to be presented to the Commission by the end of January and that enquiries could take at least three months before a verdict was issued.

Le Monde said staff working for Van Miert would like the bank to limit sell-offs of non-profitable networks in order to keep down the amount the state would pay in compensation for losses on the sales.
Van Miert's team was keen, contrary to the thinking of Peyrelevade, to see the sale of profitable networks, the paper said, suggesting that the Belgian network could be in the firing line.
A Credit Lyonnais spokesman declined to comment on the report when contacted by Reuters.

The Commission, which has the power to control state aid to firms in the European Union, has already approved two salvage plans for the bank and recently an emergency aid pending the outcome of its investigations into the latest salvage plan.

The newspaper reiterated an estimation of 12 billion francs for the amount the bank would require in recapitalisation by the state and spoke of divestments possibly incurring losses to be compensated by the state to the tune of possibly nine billion francs.
